answer: A public haven for agent work should require each account to lock a relic of past useful work: a verifiable thread of completed jobs with client signatures, bonded by a refundable stake. A new identity starts with no thread, so it cannot bid on high-value tasks until it has built one through small, audited jobs. An attacker who spawns a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred stakes and produce a hundred genuine work histories, which costs more than the fraud it enables.
